name: Amazon EC2
summary: Run virtual machines with control over the operating system and runtime.
points: Use for custom software, specialized hardware or persistent processes.
Choose instance capacity to match CPU, memory and storage needs.
You manage operating-system patching and workload security.

name: AWS Lambda
summary: Run event-triggered code without managing servers.
points: Use for APIs, file processing and queue consumers.
Connect triggers such as S3, SQS and API Gateway.
Make handlers safe to retry; invocations have a maximum runtime.

name: Amazon ECS
summary: Deploy and operate containerized applications on AWS.
points: Task definitions describe container configuration and resource needs.
Services maintain the desired number of healthy tasks.
Run on Fargate or EC2; give applications scoped task roles.

name: Amazon EKS
summary: Run Kubernetes with an AWS-managed control plane.
points: Use when Kubernetes APIs, operators or tooling are required.
Deploy workloads using standard Kubernetes resources.
Plan workload security, upgrades and compute capacity explicitly.

name: AWS Fargate
summary: Provide managed compute capacity for containers.
points: Runs ECS tasks and supported EKS workloads.
Removes the need to provision and patch container hosts.
Choose requested CPU and memory carefully for each workload.

name: AWS App Runner
summary: Deploy a web application or API as a managed HTTPS service.
points: Accepts supported source repositories or container images.
Handles deployment, request routing and scaling.
Check runtime and networking requirements before choosing it.

name: Amazon S3
summary: Store and retrieve objects such as files, media and datasets.
points: Use buckets and object keys to organize content.
Versioning and lifecycle rules support recovery and retention.
Control access with IAM and bucket policies; avoid unintended public access.

name: Amazon EBS
summary: Provide persistent block storage for EC2 workloads.
points: Use for operating-system disks and application data volumes.
Select volume performance for the workload's I/O requirements.
Use snapshots for recovery; account for Availability Zone placement.

name: Amazon EFS
summary: Provide a shared managed file system for Linux workloads.
points: Multiple clients can access files over NFS.
Use for applications needing shared file paths.
Configure access points, network access and throughput for the workload.

name: Amazon S3 Glacier
summary: Archive infrequently accessed objects in S3 storage classes.
points: Choose a class according to retrieval speed and access frequency.
Lifecycle rules move eligible objects into archival storage.
Consider retrieval charges and minimum storage durations.

name: Amazon RDS
summary: Operate a relational database with managed infrastructure tasks.
points: Use SQL, relational schemas and transactions.
AWS handles supported backup and maintenance operations.
Plan availability, recovery and database access controls.

name: Amazon Aurora
summary: Run an AWS-managed relational database compatible with MySQL or PostgreSQL.
points: Use for relational applications needing managed replication and scaling.
Separate writer and reader workloads where appropriate.
Check engine compatibility and capacity requirements before migrating.

name: Amazon DynamoDB
summary: Store key-value and document data with managed scaling.
points: Design partition and sort keys around access patterns.
Use indexes for supported alternative queries.
Avoid hot keys and unbounded scans; design consistent update rules.

name: Amazon ElastiCache
summary: Serve frequently accessed data from an in-memory cache.
points: Use for sessions, cached queries and rate-limiting state.
Choose a supported engine and appropriate deployment mode.
Set expiration and invalidation rules to prevent stale results.

name: Amazon VPC
summary: Define an isolated network for AWS resources.
points: Subnets and routes determine how traffic moves.
Security groups control allowed resource traffic.
Use appropriate gateways or endpoints for external and AWS service access.

name: Amazon Route 53
summary: Resolve domain names and route DNS traffic.
points: Host public or private DNS zones.
Use routing policies and health checks for suitable failover designs.
Account for DNS caching when planning changes.

name: Amazon CloudFront
summary: Deliver content through a global edge network.
points: Cache static assets and suitable application responses.
Configure cache keys so users receive the correct content variant.
Use Origin Access Control when serving private S3 origins.

name: Elastic Load Balancing
summary: Distribute incoming traffic across healthy application targets.
points: Choose a load-balancer type for the required protocol.
Health checks determine which targets receive traffic.
Use routing and Availability Zone coverage appropriate to the application.

name: AWS Direct Connect
summary: Connect an on-premises network to AWS through dedicated connectivity.
points: Use for predictable private network connectivity.
Virtual interfaces support different destination types.
Plan redundant connections and encryption requirements separately.

name: Amazon API Gateway
summary: Publish and manage application APIs.
points: Route HTTP, REST or WebSocket requests to supported backends.
Configure authorization, throttling and request handling.
Monitor failures and latency at both gateway and backend.

name: AWS IAM
summary: Control who can access AWS resources and what they can do.
points: Use roles and policies for workload permissions.
Prefer temporary credentials and least privilege.
Evaluate explicit denies and organization policies when troubleshooting access.

name: AWS Secrets Manager
summary: Store and retrieve application secrets securely.
points: Use for database credentials and API secrets.
Supports rotation workflows for compatible integrations.
Restrict retrieval permissions and avoid writing secrets into logs.

name: AWS KMS
summary: Manage encryption keys and control their use.
points: Integrates with encryption in many AWS services.
Key policies and IAM govern encryption and decryption access.
Plan key retention carefully so encrypted data remains recoverable.

name: Amazon GuardDuty
summary: Detect suspicious activity in supported AWS data sources.
points: Produces findings for potentially malicious behavior.
Route findings into investigation and response workflows.
Review severity and context before deciding on remediation.

name: AWS Shield
summary: Protect supported AWS resources against distributed denial-of-service attacks.
points: Standard and Advanced provide different protection capabilities.
Use alongside resilient networking and application design.
Application-layer request filtering is a separate WAF responsibility.

name: AWS WAF
summary: Filter web requests using application-layer rules.
points: Use managed or custom rules for common attack patterns.
Rate-based rules help control abusive request volume.
Test rules in count mode before blocking legitimate users.

name: Amazon Cognito
summary: Add user sign-in and identity integration to applications.
points: User pools manage application users and authentication flows.
Identity pools can provide temporary AWS credentials.
Resource authorization still belongs in the application and its policies.

name: Amazon CloudWatch
summary: Observe application and infrastructure behavior.
points: Collect metrics, logs and operational signals.
Alarms notify responders when configured conditions occur.
Build dashboards around user impact and actionable signals.

name: AWS X-Ray
summary: Trace requests across distributed application components.
points: Use traces to identify latency and downstream failures.
Instrument services and propagate trace context.
Apply sampling and avoid recording sensitive payloads.

name: AWS CloudTrail
summary: Record AWS account activity for audit and investigation.
points: Shows who performed supported API actions and when.
Configure additional event coverage where required.
Store audit records with appropriate retention and access restrictions.

name: AWS Systems Manager
summary: Operate and configure managed compute resources.
points: Supports session access, patching and automation workflows.
Parameter Store holds configuration and supported secure parameters.
Scope operator permissions and record operational changes.

name: AWS CloudFormation
summary: Provision AWS infrastructure from declarative templates.
points: Manage related resources as stacks.
Review change sets before applying infrastructure changes.
Track drift and protect stateful resources during updates.

name: AWS CDK
summary: Define cloud infrastructure using programming languages.
points: Constructs compose reusable infrastructure definitions.
Synthesizes templates for CloudFormation deployment.
Review generated changes and keep deployment roles restricted.

name: AWS Config
summary: Track resource configuration and evaluate configured rules.
points: Retains configuration history for supported resources.
Rules identify configuration drift from expected policy.
Remediation requires a defined action or automation workflow.

name: AWS Organizations
summary: Manage multiple AWS accounts under one organization.
points: Group accounts into organizational units.
Service control policies limit available permissions.
Policies set boundaries; they do not grant access themselves.

name: AWS Budgets & Cost Explorer
summary: Plan cloud spending and understand cost patterns.
points: Budgets alert on configured cost or usage thresholds.
Cost Explorer helps analyze historical spending.
Budget alerts do not automatically stop resource usage.

name: Amazon Athena
summary: Query supported data using SQL without managing query servers.
points: Commonly queries datasets stored in S3.
Partitioning and columnar formats can reduce scanned data.
Maintain accurate table metadata and access controls.

name: Amazon EMR
summary: Run distributed data-processing frameworks on AWS.
points: Supports workloads built with frameworks such as Spark.
Choose a deployment option for the workload's operational needs.
Tune job resources and inspect failed or skewed stages.

name: Amazon Redshift
summary: Analyze structured data in a managed data warehouse.
points: Use SQL for reporting and analytical workloads.
Organize ingestion and models around business questions.
Monitor query performance, workload isolation and data freshness.

name: Amazon Kinesis
summary: Process streams of incoming records with Kinesis Data Streams.
points: Producers write events; consumers process the stream.
Partition keys influence ordering and load distribution.
Plan retention and consumer recovery for delayed processing.

name: AWS Glue
summary: Discover, catalog and transform data for analytics.
points: The Data Catalog stores dataset metadata.
ETL jobs prepare data for downstream analysis.
Validate schema changes and data quality before publication.

name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
summary: Provide managed search, log analytics and vector-search capabilities.
points: Indexes data for low-latency retrieval.
Supports operational exploration and application search.
Plan mappings, access control, capacity and index retention.

name: Amazon Bedrock
summary: Build generative AI applications using managed foundation models.
points: Use for assistants, content generation and grounded answers.
Knowledge Bases support retrieval; Guardrails add configurable controls.
Check model availability, permissions and provider prerequisites.

name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
summary: Deploy and operate AI agents with managed infrastructure.
points: Runtime hosts agents; Memory supports retained context.
Gateway connects tools; Identity controls access.
Use policy and observability to govern and inspect agent actions.

name: Amazon SageMaker AI
summary: Build, train and deploy machine-learning models.
points: Use when custom training or model hosting is required.
Provides training jobs, deployment options and ML workflows.
Evaluate models before release and monitor production behavior.

name: Amazon Q
summary: Assist users with AWS work and enterprise information.
points: Q Business answers questions over configured enterprise sources.
Q Developer assists with AWS tasks in supported experiences.
Developer IDE plugins reach end of support on 30 April 2027; review the migration notice.

name: Amazon Rekognition
summary: Analyze images and videos with managed computer vision.
points: Detect labels, text and supported content categories.
Use for media organization and moderation workflows.
Review confidence thresholds and permission to process personal imagery.

name: Amazon Textract
summary: Extract text and structured fields from documents.
points: Recognizes supported forms, tables and document layouts.
Use for invoice, application and document-processing pipelines.
Validate extracted fields and route uncertain results to review.

name: Amazon Transcribe
summary: Convert speech into text.
points: Supports batch and streaming transcription workflows.
Custom vocabulary can improve recognition of domain terms.
Check supported languages and review accuracy on representative audio.

name: Amazon Polly
summary: Convert written text into spoken audio.
points: Use for read-aloud features and voice interfaces.
Supported voices and SSML control aspects of speech output.
Check voice, language and engine compatibility.

name: Amazon Comprehend
summary: Identify useful information in text using natural-language processing.
points: Extract supported entities, key phrases and sentiment.
Use for document tagging and text-analysis pipelines.
Evaluate language support and confidence for the intended task.

name: Amazon Translate
summary: Translate text between supported languages.
points: Use for multilingual content and application workflows.
Custom terminology helps preserve preferred domain terms.
Review important translations for meaning and context.

name: Amazon Lex
summary: Build conversational interfaces using voice or text.
points: Define intents, slots and fulfillment actions.
Use for structured tasks such as booking or support routing.
Handle unrecognized requests and missing information explicitly.

name: Amazon Personalize
summary: Generate recommendations from user interaction data.
points: Use for personalized item discovery and ranking.
Train on supported interaction, user and item datasets.
Evaluate recommendation quality and keep event data current.

name: Amazon Forecast
summary: Generate forecasts from historical time-series data.
points: Applies to supported demand and resource-planning use cases.
Closed to new customers since 29 July 2024.
New projects should evaluate supported alternatives such as SageMaker Canvas.

name: Amazon Kendra
summary: Search enterprise content using natural-language queries.
points: Connects and indexes supported repositories.
Use for internal knowledge discovery and document retrieval.
Configure identity and document permissions to protect restricted results.

name: AWS CodePipeline
summary: Orchestrate software-release stages.
points: Connect source, build, test and deployment actions.
Use approvals where a release decision requires review.
Promote a tested artifact and define a recovery path.

name: AWS CodeBuild
summary: Run builds and tests in managed build environments.
points: A buildspec defines commands and output artifacts.
Use for compilation, automated checks and image builds.
Protect secrets and restrict the build service role.

name: AWS CodeDeploy
summary: Automate deployments to supported compute targets.
points: Supports deployment strategies for EC2, Lambda and ECS.
Health checks and alarms can support rollback decisions.
Test deployment hooks and recovery before production releases.

name: AWS CodeArtifact
summary: Store and distribute software packages.
points: Use private repositories for supported package formats.
Configure upstream sources for dependency retrieval.
Control publishing permissions and dependency versions.

name: AWS CodeCommit
summary: Host private Git repositories in AWS.
points: Use Git workflows with AWS access controls.
Repositories can connect to supported delivery pipelines.
Check current account availability before adopting the service.

name: Amazon ECR
summary: Store and distribute container images.
points: Build systems push images; runtimes pull them.
Use image scanning and lifecycle policies.
Deploy immutable image digests for reproducible releases.

name: AWS AppConfig
summary: Release application configuration and feature flags safely.
points: Separate configuration rollout from code deployment.
Validate configuration before release.
Use gradual rollout and monitoring to detect harmful changes.

name: AWS OpsWorks
summary: Understand legacy AWS configuration-management deployments.
points: Historically managed infrastructure with Chef and Puppet workflows.
The OpsWorks offerings have reached end of life.
Use supported management tools when designing new infrastructure.

name: Amazon DevOps Guru
summary: Detect operational anomalies using machine learning.
points: Analyzes supported application and infrastructure signals.
Insights help prioritize investigation of abnormal behavior.
Validate findings against application context before changing resources.

name: Amazon SQS
summary: Decouple producers and workers with a managed message queue.
points: Use for asynchronous work and buffering traffic spikes.
Visibility timeouts protect messages while workers process them.
Design retry-safe consumers and a dead-letter-queue policy.

name: Amazon SNS
summary: Distribute published messages to multiple subscribers.
points: Use for notifications and event fan-out.
Supports several endpoint types, including SQS and Lambda.
Configure delivery, retry and subscription permissions.

name: Amazon EventBridge
summary: Route events between applications and supported services.
points: Rules match event patterns and forward to targets.
Use for loosely coupled application workflows.
Define event contracts and failure-handling destinations.

name: AWS Step Functions
summary: Coordinate multi-step workflows with explicit state.
points: Connect supported service tasks, branches and parallel work.
Configure retries, timeouts and error handling.
Choose the workflow type for execution and durability needs.

name: Amazon Data Firehose
summary: Deliver streaming data to supported destinations.
points: Buffers incoming records before delivery.
Can transform or convert supported data before writing.
Monitor delivery failures and configure backup destinations.

name: AWS Global Accelerator
summary: Improve access to regional applications through the AWS global network.
points: Provides static anycast IP addresses.
Routes traffic to configured healthy endpoints.
Use for network routing; CloudFront serves content-caching needs.

name: AWS Batch
summary: Schedule and execute batch-computing jobs.
points: Job queues organize work by priority and requirements.
Compute environments provide capacity for queued jobs.
Set resource requests, retry rules and execution limits.
